item.title: Building Shiny Apps
item.description: The goal of this workshop is to introduce participants to the development of interactive web applications using Shiny in R. The workshop helps participants understand what Shiny is, how it enables the creation of interactive dashboards and data-exploration tools, and how applications are structured. Participants learn key concepts such as reactive programming, the architecture of Shiny applications, and how user inputs and outputs interact to produce dynamic visualizations and analytical tools.

item.title: Teamwork with git & GitHub
item.description: The goal of this workshop is to introduce participants to the fundamentals of version control using Git and collaborative development using platforms such as GitHub. The workshop focuses on helping participants understand how to track changes in code, data, and documents over time, allowing them to safely manage project history, recover from mistakes, and maintain organized and transparent analytical workflows. Participants typically learn core concepts such as repositories, commits, and project versioning, which are considered essential components of modern research and data-science practices.

item.title: Working on rasters with R
item.description:
The goal of this workshop is to introduce participants to the fundamentals of manipulating, analyzing, and visualizing raster data using R, with an emphasis on reproducible workflows tailored to environmental spatial analysis needs. Through demonstrations and hands-on exercises, the workshop helps participants become familiar with key tools and concepts used to load, explore, transform, and visualize gridded spatial data, while promoting good practices in organizing code and data.

More broadly, the workshop aims to strengthen participants’ capacity to integrate spatial data into scientific analyses or environmental management workflows. It focuses on understanding raster data structures, using them to produce meaningful visualizations, and incorporating them into reproducible analytical pipelines. By the end of the workshop, participants should be able to apply these approaches to their own projects, particularly for exploring, summarizing, and communicating spatial data related to biodiversity or habitat management.

item.title: Reproducible Workflows
item.description: The goal of this workshop is to introduce participants to the principles and practical tools needed to conduct reproducible research using R. The workshop focuses on helping participants understand how to organize data, code, and analyses so that results can be reliably reproduced by others or by themselves in the future. Participants learn how to integrate documentation, data processing, and reporting within structured workflows that improve transparency, collaboration, and long-term project sustainability. Reproducible workflows ensure that when the same data and code are used, the same results can be obtained, which is considered a fundamental standard of scientific and analytical work.

item.title: Interactive raster visualization with R
item.description: The goal of this workshop is to introduce participants to the development of interactive tools for exploring and visualizing raster-based spatial data in R. Through guided exercises, participants learn how to move beyond static maps by building interactive dashboards that allow users to pan, zoom, click, and otherwise engage with spatial layers dynamically. The workshop emphasizes using modern mapping libraries such as leaflet and tmap, and helps participants assemble these components into shareable, browser-based outputs, including HTML dashboards and simple Shiny applications.
